scope: Exodus 9–11, all 74 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Exodus 9–11.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains the recurring divine speech formula, named relationship, and release-for-service demand with the warning continuing across labels.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and speak to him: ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him, ‘This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go so they may serve me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and speak to him: ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, that they may serve me.

verses.rationale: Preserves both refusal and continued detention as the condition, leaving its result in the next verse within the same paragraph.
verses.before: For if you refuse to let them go and still hold them,
verses.after: If you refuse to let them go and keep holding them,
verses.tsw_comparator: For if you refuse to let them go and still hold them,

verses.rationale: Retains the divine hand, the field qualification, and every livestock category, rendering the collective flock term as sheep and goats.
verses.before: look: the hand of the LORD will be against your livestock in the field—against the horses, the donkeys, the camels, the herds, and the flocks—a very severe plague.
verses.after: the LORD’s hand will fall on your livestock in the fields—horses, donkeys, camels, cattle, sheep, and goats—with a very severe plague.
verses.tsw_comparator: look: the hand of the LORD will be against your livestock in the field—against the horses, the donkeys, the camels, the herds, and the flocks—a very severe plague.

verses.rationale: Keeps the explicit distinction and absolute promise within the stated livestock context.
verses.before: But the LORD will make a distinction between Israel’s livestock and Egypt’s livestock; not one thing belonging to the Israelites will die.’”
verses.after: But the LORD will distinguish between Israel’s livestock and Egypt’s. Not one animal belonging to the Israelites will die.”’”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD will make a distinction between Israel’s livestock and Egypt’s livestock; not one thing belonging to the Israelites will die.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the appointed tomorrow and the divine name in the third person within the speech.
verses.before: And the LORD set an appointed time, saying, “Tomorrow the LORD will do this thing in the land.”
verses.after: The LORD set a time: “Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD set an appointed time, saying, “Tomorrow the LORD will do this thing in the land.”

verses.rationale: Retains all without silently reducing it to many or adding the field qualification not repeated in this verse; a note identifies the narrative tension with later animals.
verses.before: The next day the LORD did this thing: all the livestock of Egypt died, but not one of the livestock of the Israelites died.
verses.after: The next day the LORD did it. All Egypt’s livestock died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.
verses.tsw_comparator: The next day the LORD did this thing: all the livestock of Egypt died, but not one of the livestock of the Israelites died.

verses.rationale: Supplies the contextual purpose of sending and preserves the heavy-heart state without naming a causing agent.
verses.before: Pharaoh sent, and look: not even one of Israel’s livestock had died. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he did not let the people go.
verses.after: Pharaoh sent people to find out, and indeed, not a single animal belonging to Israel had died. Yet Pharaoh’s heart was unyielding, and he did not let the people go.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh sent, and look: not even one of Israel’s livestock had died. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he did not let the people go.

verses.rationale: Keeps both men gathering soot and Moses specifically throwing it, without identifying the kiln as a particular industrial or ritual installation.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Take for yourselves handfuls of soot from a furnace, and let Moses throw it toward the heavens in Pharaoh’s sight.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Fill your hands with soot from a kiln. Moses is to throw it toward the sky before Pharaoh’s eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Take for yourselves handfuls of soot from a furnace, and let Moses throw it toward the heavens in Pharaoh’s sight.

verses.rationale: Preserves the progression from soot to dust to bodily lesions and both affected groups without a modern disease diagnosis.
verses.before: It will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and it will become festering boils on people and animals throughout all the land of Egypt.”
verses.after: It will become fine dust over all Egypt and cause boils to break out in blisters on people and animals throughout the land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and it will become festering boils on people and animals throughout all the land of Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the plural preparation, singular throwing, and repeated bodily effects in the fulfillment.
verses.before: So they took soot from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh. Moses threw it toward the heavens, and it became festering boils on people and animals.
verses.after: They took soot from the kiln and stood before Pharaoh. Moses threw it toward the sky, and boils broke out in blisters on people and animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they took soot from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh. Moses threw it toward the heavens, and it became festering boils on people and animals.

verses.rationale: Retains the specialists’ bodily incapacity alongside the wider suffering without recasting it as merely loss of status.
verses.before: The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were on the magicians and on all the Egyptians.
verses.after: The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils. They had broken out on the magicians and all the Egyptians.
verses.tsw_comparator: The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were on the magicians and on all the Egyptians.

verses.rationale: Keeps the LORD explicitly as the hardening agent in this fulfillment and clarifies the hearers while retaining the prior-prediction formula.
verses.before: But the LORD strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses.
verses.after: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had told Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves the renewed morning command and complete recurring demand rather than compressing the repetition.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning, stand before Pharaoh, and say to him, ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh. Tell him, ‘This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go so they may serve me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning, stand before Pharaoh, and say to him, ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, that they may serve me.

verses.rationale: Retains the heart image, all three recipients, and the stated knowing purpose rather than treating the heart as an anatomical target only.
verses.before: For this time I am sending all my plagues against your heart, against your servants, and against your people, so that you may know that there is none like me in all the earth.
verses.after: This time I will send all my plagues against your very heart, and against your servants and your people, so you may know that there is no one like me in all the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this time I am sending all my plagues against your heart, against your servants, and against your people, so that you may know that there is none like me in all the earth.

verses.rationale: Renders the unrealized possibility in context, not a claim that Pharaoh has already been exterminated.
verses.before: For by now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with plague, and you would have been cut off from the earth.
verses.after: By now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with plague, wiping you from the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: For by now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with plague, and you would have been cut off from the earth.

verses.rationale: Retains the standing image and both purposes, with the spare/establish range noted rather than replacing the statement with a later quotation.
verses.before: Yet for this reason I have made you stand: to show you my power, and so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth.
verses.after: But I have kept you standing for this purpose: to show you my power and have my name proclaimed throughout the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet for this reason I have made you stand: to show you my power, and so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth.

verses.rationale: Renders the self-exalting obstruction in natural English while preserving Pharaoh’s continued opposition as his own action.
verses.before: Do you still exalt yourself over my people, refusing to let them go?
verses.after: You still set yourself above my people and refuse to let them go.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you still exalt yourself over my people, refusing to let them go?

verses.rationale: Keeps the approximate time and full historical comparison without assigning a date to Egypt’s founding.
verses.before: Look: about this time tomorrow I will rain down very heavy hail, such as has never been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.
verses.after: About this time tomorrow I will rain down hail so severe that Egypt has never seen its like, from the day it was founded until now.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look: about this time tomorrow I will rain down very heavy hail, such as has never been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.

verses.rationale: Preserves the protective warning, all possessions, and explicit death of exposed people and animals without muting the harm.
verses.before: Now send word; bring your livestock and all that you have in the field under shelter. Every person and animal found in the field and not gathered into the house—when the hail comes down on them—will die.’”
verses.after: Now send word to bring your livestock and everything you have in the fields into shelter. Every person or animal left outside and not brought indoors will be struck by hail and die.”’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now send word; bring your livestock and all that you have in the field under shelter. Every person and animal found in the field and not gathered into the house—when the hail comes down on them—will die.’”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Pharaoh’s court servants from the people under their control, retaining both fear and protective action.
verses.before: Whoever among Pharaoh’s servants feared the word of the LORD brought their servants and livestock into the houses.
verses.after: Those among Pharaoh’s servants who feared the LORD’s word hurried their slaves and livestock indoors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever among Pharaoh’s servants feared the word of the LORD brought their servants and livestock into the houses.

verses.rationale: Keeps the heart idiom, the contrasting failure to act, and the exposure of dependent people and animals.
verses.before: But whoever did not set their heart on the word of the LORD left their servants and livestock in the field.
verses.after: Those who did not take the LORD’s word to heart left their slaves and livestock in the fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: But whoever did not set their heart on the word of the LORD left their servants and livestock in the field.

verses.rationale: Retains the command’s skyward direction and the full human, animal, and plant scope.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, that there may be hail throughout all the land of Egypt—upon people, animals, and every plant of the field in the land of Egypt.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky so hail falls throughout Egypt—on people, animals, and every plant in the fields.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, that there may be hail throughout all the land of Egypt—upon people, animals, and every plant of the field in the land of Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses’ gesture distinct from the LORD’s action and retains fire as the ancient storm image rather than replacing all occurrences with lightning.
verses.before: Moses stretched out his staff toward the heavens, and the LORD gave thunder and hail, and fire ran down to the earth. The LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Moses stretched his staff toward the sky. The LORD sent thunder and hail, and fire flashed down to the earth. The LORD rained hail on Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses stretched out his staff toward the heavens, and the LORD gave thunder and hail, and fire ran down to the earth. The LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves interwoven hail and fire and the repeated national-history comparison.
verses.before: There was hail, and fire flashing among the hail, very severe—such as had never been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
verses.after: Hail fell, with fire flashing through it. The storm was so severe that nothing like it had happened in Egypt since it became a nation.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was hail, and fire flashing in the midst of the hail, very severe—such as had never been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.

verses.rationale: Retains comprehensive field destruction across human, animal, plant, and tree categories without extending the scope to those sheltered indoors.
verses.before: The hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt everything that was in the field, from people to animals. The hail struck every plant of the field and shattered every tree of the field.
verses.after: Throughout Egypt the hail struck everything in the fields, both people and animals. It battered every plant in the fields and shattered every tree.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt everything that was in the field, from people to animals. The hail struck every plant of the field and shattered every tree of the field.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sole named geographical exception without supplying a meteorological explanation.
verses.before: Only in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites were, was there no hail.
verses.after: Only Goshen, where the Israelites were, had no hail.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites were, was there no hail.

verses.rationale: Preserves Pharaoh’s confession, its this-time qualification, and the righteous/wrong contrast as his own words.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh sent and called for Moses and Aaron. He said to them, “I have sinned this time. The LORD is righteous; I and my people are wicked.
verses.after: Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron. “This time I have sinned,” he told them. “The LORD is righteous; my people and I are in the wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh sent and called for Moses and Aaron. He said to them, “I have sinned this time. The LORD is righteous; I and my people are wicked.

verses.rationale: Retains the possible divine genitive in thunder, the appeal, and the renewed release promise rather than explaining his sincerity.
verses.before: Plead with the LORD, for there has been enough of God’s thunder and hail. I will let you go, and you will not remain any longer.”
verses.after: Plead with the LORD. We have had enough of God’s thunder and hail! I will let you go; you will not have to stay any longer.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Plead with the LORD, for there has been enough of God’s thunder and hail. I will let you go, and you will not remain any longer.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the promised location and prayer gesture, both weather changes, and the wider ownership claim.
verses.before: Moses said to him, “When I have gone out of the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD. The thunder will cease, and the hail will be no more, so that you may know that the earth belongs to the LORD.
verses.after: Moses said, “As soon as I leave the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD. The thunder will stop, and there will be no more hail, so you may know that the earth belongs to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to him, “When I have gone out of the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD. The thunder will cease, and the hail will be no more, so that you may know that the earth belongs to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains Moses’ explicit assessment and not-yet qualification without expanding it into a doctrine of repentance.
verses.before: But as for you and your servants, I know that you still will not fear the LORD God.”
verses.after: But I know that you and your servants do not yet fear the LORD God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for you and your servants, I know that you still will not fear the LORD God.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the narrator’s crop aside and each crop’s distinct growth stage without confusing barley with later wheat.
verses.before: Now the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in ear and the flax was in bloom.
verses.after: The flax and barley had been struck down: the barley was in the ear, and the flax was in bud.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in ear and the flax was in bloom.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit crop exceptions and later growth, using the conventional spelt identification with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they were late crops.
verses.after: But the wheat and spelt were not struck down because they ripen later.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they were late crops.

verses.rationale: Keeps the completed location and gesture, thunder and hail cessation, and the additional rain detail.
verses.before: Then Moses went out from Pharaoh, out of the city, and spread out his hands to the LORD. The thunder and the hail ceased, and rain did not pour down upon the earth.
verses.after: Moses left Pharaoh and went out of the city. He spread out his hands to the LORD, and the thunder and hail stopped. Rain no longer poured onto the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses went out from Pharaoh, out of the city, and spread out his hands to the LORD. The thunder and the hail ceased, and rain did not pour down upon the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves Pharaoh’s renewed sin and the servants’ participation, rendering the Hebrew singular heart with the shared subject in natural English.
verses.before: But when Pharaoh saw that the rain, the hail, and the thunder had ceased, he continued to sin, and he made his heart heavy—he and his servants.
verses.after: When Pharaoh saw that the rain, hail, and thunder had stopped, he sinned again. He and his servants hardened their hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Pharaoh saw that the rain, the hail, and the thunder had ceased, he continued to sin, and he made his heart heavy—he and his servants.

verses.rationale: Keeps the uncaused grammatical state and the mediated-word formula, distinct from the named agents in the preceding verse.
verses.before: Pharaoh’s heart was strengthened, and he did not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had spoken through Moses.
verses.after: Pharaoh’s heart remained hard, and he did not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh’s heart was strengthened, and he did not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had spoken through Moses.

verses.rationale: Keeps God as the explicit agent acting on both Pharaoh and servants, and lets the purpose continue into the next verse.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have made his heart heavy, and the hearts of his servants, so that I may set these signs of mine among them,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh. I have hardened his heart and his servants’ hearts so that I may perform these signs among them,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have made his heart heavy, and the hearts of his servants, so that I may set these signs of mine among them,

verses.rationale: Retains the force of the harsh-treatment verb, specifically named male generations, and the shift from singular storyteller to plural knowing audience.
verses.before: and so that you may recount in the hearing of your child and of your child’s child how I dealt harshly with Egypt, and my signs that I set among them, and you may know that I am the LORD.”
verses.after: and so that you may tell your son and your grandson how I made a mockery of Egypt and what signs I performed among them. Then you all will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and so that you may recount in the hearing of your child and of your child’s child how I dealt harshly with Egypt, and my signs that I set among them, and you may know that I am the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both messengers, the how-long challenge, and the demand’s repeated purpose without reducing humbling to private feeling.
verses.before: So Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh and said to him, “Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Send my people away, that they may serve me.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go so they may serve me.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh and said to him, “Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Send my people away, that they may serve me.

verses.rationale: Retains the conditional warning and the named next-day onset.
verses.before: For if you refuse to send my people away, look, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your territory.
verses.after: If you refuse to let my people go, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if you refuse to send my people away, look, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your territory.

verses.rationale: Renders eye-of-the-land as face of the land while preserving visual coverage and the direct link with surviving hail-damaged vegetation.
verses.before: They will cover the face of the land, so that no one will be able to see the land. They will eat the remainder of what escaped—the part left for you from the hail—and they will eat every tree that grows for you from the field.
verses.after: They will cover the face of the land so no one can see the ground. They will eat whatever the hail left for you, and every tree growing in your fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will cover the face of the land, so that no one will be able to see the land. They will eat the remainder of what escaped—the part left for you from the hail—and they will eat every tree that grows for you from the field.

verses.rationale: Retains all household groups and the ancestral comparison, preserving fathers and their fathers while making the singular departing speaker clear.
verses.before: They will fill your houses, the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all Egypt—something your ancestors and your ancestors’ ancestors have never seen from the day they came to be upon the earth until this day.” Then he turned and went out from Pharaoh’s presence.
verses.after: They will fill your houses, all your servants’ houses, and every Egyptian house—something neither your fathers nor their fathers have seen in all their days on the earth.’” Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will fill your houses, the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all Egypt—something your ancestors and your ancestors’ ancestors have never seen from the day they came to be upon the earth until this day.” Then he turned and went out from Pharaoh’s presence.

verses.rationale: Retains the snare image, the servants’ restriction to men, and their recognition of destruction as a challenge to Pharaoh.
verses.before: Pharaoh’s servants said to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Send the men away, that they may serve the LORD their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt is ruined?”
verses.after: Pharaoh’s servants said to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the men go to serve the LORD their God. Do you still not realize that Egypt is ruined?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh’s servants said to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Send the men away, that they may serve the LORD their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt is ruined?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the passive return and renders who-and-who as a pointed demand for the composition of the departing group.
verses.before: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, “Go, serve the LORD your God. But who exactly are the ones going?”
verses.after: Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go and serve the LORD your God,” he said. “But exactly who is going?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, “Go, serve the LORD your God. But who exactly are the ones going?”

verses.rationale: Preserves every age, gender, and animal category in Moses’ answer, countering the proposed departure of men only.
verses.before: Moses said, “We will go with our young and our old; we will go with our sons and our daughters, with our flocks and our herds, for we have a festival of the LORD.”
verses.after: Moses answered, “We will go with our young and old, our sons and daughters, our flocks and herds. We have a festival to keep for the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said, “We will go with our young and our old; we will go with our sons and our daughters, with our flocks and our herds, for we have a festival of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Retains the sarcastic conditional blessing and the ambiguous evil-before-you warning, with an alternative reference to their intentions noted.
verses.before: He said to them, “May LORD be with you in that way, if I send you and your little ones! See: disaster is before you.
verses.after: Pharaoh said, “May the LORD be with you—if I ever let you and your little ones go! Watch out: evil lies ahead of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “May LORD be with you in that way, if I send you and your little ones! See: disaster is before you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicitly male restriction and forced dismissal without specifying an unnamed court official as the expeller.
verses.before: Not so! Go now, you men, and serve the LORD, for that is what you are seeking.” And he drove them from Pharaoh’s presence.
verses.after: No! You men may go and serve the LORD, since that is what you are asking for.” Moses and Aaron were driven out of Pharaoh’s presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not so! Go now, you men, and serve the LORD, for that is what you are seeking.” And he drove them from Pharaoh’s presence.

verses.rationale: Keeps the command linked to locust arrival and repeats the surviving-after-hail scope.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up over the land of Egypt and eat every plant of the land, all that the hail left.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over Egypt for the locusts to come up and eat every plant in the land, everything the hail has left.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up over the land of Egypt and eat every plant of the land, all that the hail left.”

verses.rationale: Retains the LORD’s wind agency, east direction, full day and night, and arrival by morning.
verses.before: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and the LORD drove an east wind over the land all that day and all that night. When morning came, the east wind had carried in the locusts.
verses.after: Moses stretched his staff over Egypt, and the LORD drove an east wind across the land all that day and all night. Morning came, and the east wind had carried in the locusts.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and the LORD drove an east wind over the land all that day and all that night. When morning came, the east wind had carried in the locusts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the complete territorial coverage and the narrator’s past-and-future superlative without weakening it to within living memory.
verses.before: The locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled throughout all the territory of Egypt. They were very severe; never before had there been locusts like them, nor would there ever be again.
verses.after: The locusts spread over all Egypt and settled throughout its territory in a vast swarm. There had never been locusts like them before, and there would never be again.
verses.tsw_comparator: The locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled throughout all the territory of Egypt. They were very severe; never before had there been locusts like them, nor would there ever be again.

verses.rationale: Preserves darkened land, all fruit and plants left by hail, and the emphatic absence of green growth.
verses.before: They covered the face of the whole land, and the land grew dark. They ate every plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left. Nothing green remained on any tree or among the plants of the field in all the land of Egypt.
verses.after: They covered the face of the whole land until it was dark. They ate every plant and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left. Nothing green remained on any tree or plant in the fields throughout Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: They covered the face of the whole land, and the land grew dark. They ate every plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left. Nothing green remained on any tree or among the plants of the field in all the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains urgency and both objects of the confession without adding an assessment of the speaker’s sincerity.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh hurried to call Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
verses.after: Pharaoh hurriedly summoned Moses and Aaron. “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you,” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh hurried to call Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two restrictive appeals and Pharaoh’s death image rather than replacing it with a mild inconvenience.
verses.before: Now, please, bear my sin just this once, and plead with the LORD your God, that he may remove from me only this death.”
verses.after: “Please forgive my sin just this once. Plead with the LORD your God to take only this death away from me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now, please, bear my sin just this once, and plead with the LORD your God, that he may remove from me only this death.”

verses.rationale: Identifies the singular departing and praying figure from the continuing narrative pattern without inventing the prayer’s wording.
verses.before: So he went out from Pharaoh’s presence and pleaded with the LORD.
verses.after: Moses left Pharaoh and pleaded with the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he went out from Pharaoh’s presence and pleaded with the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reversal from east to west, complete removal, and the Hebrew sea-name rendering, with the traditional Red Sea name noted.
verses.before: The LORD turned a very strong west wind, and it carried away the locusts and drove them into the Sea of Reeds. Not one locust remained in all the territory of Egypt.
verses.after: The LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind. It lifted the locusts and swept them into the Sea of Reeds. Not one locust remained anywhere in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD turned a very strong west wind, and it carried away the locusts and drove them into the Sea of Reeds. Not one locust remained in all the territory of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains the LORD as the explicit hardening agent after removal of the locusts.
verses.before: But the LORD strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not send the Israelites away.
verses.after: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not let the Israelites go.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not send the Israelites away.

verses.rationale: Preserves the tactile darkness image without converting it into a particular weather event or metaphor for unbelief.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt—a darkness that can be felt.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky so darkness comes over Egypt—darkness that can be felt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt—a darkness that can be felt.”

verses.rationale: Retains the gesture, intensified darkness, full geographic scope, and exact three-day period.
verses.before: So Moses stretched out his hand toward the heavens, and there was thick darkness throughout all the land of Egypt for three days.
verses.after: Moses stretched his hand toward the sky, and deep darkness covered all Egypt for three days.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses stretched out his hand toward the heavens, and there was thick darkness throughout all the land of Egypt for three days.

verses.rationale: Keeps both incapacities, repeats the three days, and preserves the explicitly universal Israelite exception.
verses.before: No one saw another, and no one rose from where they were for three days; but all the Israelites had light in their dwellings.
verses.after: No one could see anyone else or rise from where they were for three days. But all the Israelites had light where they lived.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one saw another, and no one rose from where they were for three days; but all the Israelites had light in their dwellings.

verses.rationale: Retains the new concession for dependents alongside the remaining livestock restriction, with little ones matching the earlier exchange.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh called Moses and said, “Go, serve the LORD. Only your flocks and your herds must remain behind. Your little ones may also go with you.”
verses.after: Pharaoh summoned Moses. “Go and serve the LORD,” he said. “Only your flocks and herds must stay behind. Even your little ones may go with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh called Moses and said, “Go, serve the LORD. Only your flocks and your herds must remain behind. Your little ones may also go with you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the second-person demand directed at Pharaoh and the two offering categories without silently reducing it to permission to take Israel’s own livestock.
verses.before: Yet Moses said, “You yourself must also put sacrifices and burnt offerings into our hands, and we will offer them to the LORD our God.
verses.after: Moses answered, “You yourself must provide us with sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the LORD our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses said, “You yourself must also put sacrifices and burnt offerings into our hands, and we will offer them to the LORD our God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the hoof image, all animals, and the explicit uncertainty about worship requirements before arrival.
verses.before: Our livestock too must go with us; not a hoof will remain behind. For from it we must take to serve the LORD our God, and we do not know with what we must serve the LORD until we arrive there.”
verses.after: Our livestock must go with us too. Not a hoof will be left behind. We must take from them what we need to serve the LORD our God, and we will not know how we are to serve the LORD until we get there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Our livestock too must go with us; not a hoof will remain behind. For from it we must take to serve the LORD our God, and we do not know with what we must serve the LORD until we arrive there.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both divine hardening and Pharaoh’s unwillingness without transferring either action to the other party.
verses.before: But the LORD strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to send them away.
verses.after: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and Pharaoh was unwilling to let them go.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to send them away.

verses.rationale: Retains the expulsion command, repeated face idiom, and direct threat of death.
verses.before: Pharaoh said to him, “Go away from me! Watch yourself—do not ever again see my face, for on the day you see my face, you will die.”
verses.after: Pharaoh said to Moses, “Get away from me! Be warned: do not see my face again. The day you see my face, you will die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh said to him, “Go away from me! Watch yourself—do not ever again see my face, for on the day you see my face, you will die.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the concise assent and repeated face expression, leaving the following chapter to manage the dialogue’s continuation.
verses.before: Moses said, “You have spoken rightly. I will never again see your face.”
verses.after: Moses answered, “As you say. I will not see your face again.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said, “You have spoken rightly. I will never again see your face.”

verses.rationale: Treats the divine notice as background to the final exchange, with the temporal choice noted; preserves one more and emphatic complete expulsion.
verses.before: 1 Then the LORD said to Moses, “One more blow I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. Afterward he will send you away from here. When he sends you away completely, he will drive you out from here.
verses.after: Now the LORD had said to Moses, “I will bring one more plague on Pharaoh and Egypt. After that he will let you go from here. When he does, he will drive you out completely.
verses.tsw_comparator: 1 Then the LORD said to Moses, “One more blow I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. Afterward he will send you away from here. When he sends you away completely, he will drive you out from here.

verses.rationale: Retains the matched male and female relationships and ask rather than borrow, without adding clothing not named in this verse.
verses.before: 2 Speak, please, in the hearing of the people: let each man ask his neighbor, and each woman her neighbor, for articles of silver and articles of gold.”
verses.after: Tell the people to ask for silver and gold articles—each man from his neighbor, and each woman from hers.”
verses.tsw_comparator: 2 Speak, please, in the hearing of the people: let each man ask his neighbor, and each woman her neighbor, for articles of silver and articles of gold.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the LORD’s favor-giving and Moses’ public stature as distinct observations, leaving the last people referent open in a note.
verses.before: 3 And the LORD gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians. Moreover, the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of Pharaoh’s servants and in the eyes of the people.
verses.after: The LORD gave the people favor in the Egyptians’ eyes. Moses himself was held in very high regard in Egypt, by Pharaoh’s servants and by the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: 3 And the LORD gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians. Moreover, the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of Pharaoh’s servants and in the eyes of the people.

verses.rationale: Retains the approximate midnight and the LORD’s first-person movement within Moses’ reported message.
verses.before: 4 Moses said, “Thus says the LORD: About midnight I will go out into the midst of Egypt,
verses.after: Moses said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘About midnight I will go out through Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: 4 And Moses said, “Thus says the LORD: About midnight I will go out into the midst of Egypt,

verses.rationale: Preserves the full social range, the specifically enslaved woman and her labor, all firstborn animals, and death without euphemism.
verses.before: 5 and every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh sitting on his throne to the firstborn of the slave woman behind the millstones, and every firstborn of livestock.
verses.after: Every firstborn in Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the slave woman working at the mill, and every firstborn among the animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: 5 and every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh sitting on his throne to the firstborn of the slave woman behind the millstones, and every firstborn of livestock.

verses.rationale: Keeps the collective grief and its past-and-future uniqueness without presenting the deaths as an occasion for triumph.
verses.before: 6 There will be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as has never been and such as will never again be.
verses.after: A great cry will rise throughout Egypt, unlike anything heard before or ever to be heard again.
verses.tsw_comparator: 6 There will be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as has never been and such as will never again be.

verses.rationale: Retains the dog image, both people and animals, and the plural knowing audience, closing the divine quotation before Moses speaks about himself.
verses.before: 7 But against all the children of Israel, not even a dog will sharpen its tongue, against human or animal, so that you may know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.
verses.after: Among the Israelites, though, not even a dog will growl at a person or an animal. Then you all will know that the LORD distinguishes between Egypt and Israel.’
verses.tsw_comparator: 7 But against all the children of Israel, not even a dog will sharpen its tongue, against human or animal, so that you may know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses as the first-person speaker, the servants’ bowing, the departure demand, and Moses’ explicit anger rather than assigning it to Pharaoh.
verses.before: 8 Then all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow down to me, saying, ‘Go out—you and all the people at your feet!’ After that I will go out.” And he went out from Pharaoh in burning anger.
verses.after: All these servants of yours will come down to me and bow before me, saying, ‘Leave—you and all the people who follow you!’ After that, I will leave.” Then Moses left Pharaoh in fierce anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: 8 Then all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow down to me, saying, ‘Go out—you and all the people at your feet!’ After that I will go out.” And he went out from Pharaoh in burning anger.

verses.rationale: Retains the plural you in context and the purpose of multiplied wonders without explaining away the causal claim.
verses.before: 9 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that my signs may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that my wonders may multiply in Egypt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: 9 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that my signs may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the summary’s two performers, all wonders, divine hardening, and continuing refusal as the transition to the Passover account.
verses.before: 10 Moses and Aaron performed all these signs before Pharaoh. But the LORD strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not send the children of Israel out of his land.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron performed all these wonders before Pharaoh. But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not let the Israelites leave his land.
verses.tsw_comparator: 10 Moses and Aaron performed all these signs before Pharaoh. But the LORD strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not send the children of Israel out of his land.
